features.name: share_comments_acknowledging_exceptions
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments explicitly acknowledge exceptions to a generalization (e.g. not all, not every, not always)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment decide whether, in the commenter's own assertion, it explicitly acknowledges an exception or limit to a generalization, e.g. 'not all', 'not every', 'not always', 'some but not all', 'there are exceptions'. Mere hedging without reference to exceptions, and quoted/attributed text not adopted by the commenter (e.g. quoting the OP) do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output = number of qualifying comments / total number of comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed or missing input gives null.

h0: share_comments_acknowledging_exceptions has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: A higher share_comments_acknowledging_exceptions is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). The row-level measure is the share of counter-arguments with explicit exception acknowledgment; the share (vs any/count) is an assumption. Comments are unordered, with no timing. Rows with empty comment lists get null. Association only, not causal. Comment text may contain outcome announcements; these are excluded by the prompt.
